name: Shikargah Jaali Elephant
shortDescription: Hand-carved Kadamb wood elephant with intricate Shikargah jaali panels of forest wildlife.
description: A masterpiece of Rajasthani miniature carving, this elephant is worked entirely by hand from a single block of Kadamb (Burflower) wood. Its ceremonial drape is a Shikargah panel — the traditional ‘hunting-scene’ motif — alive with deer, tigers and foliage carved in delicate open jaali (lattice) work, framed by a royal jhula saddle and finely ornamented headpiece. The warm honey tone of the natural grain and soft matte finish make it a versatile statement piece: equally at home as desk branding, in interior and home decor, as a premium corporate gift, or as a showcase and exhibition centrepiece. Each piece is individually carved, so no two are ever identical.

details.label: Use cases
details.value: Desk branding, home & interior decor, corporate gifting, showcases, exhibitions

faqs.question: Is this product handmade?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every elephant is carved entirely by hand by skilled Jaipur artisans from a single block of wood, so each piece is unique.

faqs.question: What material is it made from?
faqs.answer: It is carved from Kadamb wood, also known as the Burflower tree — a fine-grained wood prized for detailed hand-carving.

faqs.question: What is the Shikargah design?
faqs.answer: Shikargah is a traditional hunting-scene motif. Here it is rendered as intricate open jaali (lattice) panels filled with carved deer, tigers and foliage.

faqs.question: What sizes are available?
faqs.answer: Standard sizes are 3, 4, 5 and 6 inches. Larger pieces up to 12 inches can be made on demand.

faqs.question: Do you offer bulk pricing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Single pieces are ₹700 each. For bulk orders with a minimum order quantity of 50, the price is ₹500 per piece.

faqs.question: Can the piece be customised?
faqs.answer: Yes, side customisation is available. Both single-piece and bulk orders can be accommodated.

faqs.question: How do I care for it?
faqs.answer: Dust gently with a dry, soft cloth and keep away from direct sunlight and moisture to preserve the natural grain.
